newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's women lobby for political representation.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's women lobby for political representation.

text.p: Five Moroccan women associations said on Wednesday they had set up a coordination committee to lobby for more representation in local and legislative elections from June 13.
"The women's five-member committee calls for a balanced female representation in next elections," the group said in a statement.
Only two women are represented in the existing 333-seats parliament.

Among the five-member group, the Union de l'Action Feminine, led by Latifa Jebabdi -- a left-wing militant and former political detainee -- is one of the most active associations struggling for women's rights in the Moslem kingdom.
More than 13 million voters, or nearly half Morocco's population, will be called on June 13 to elect members for 1,600 communal and municipal councils.

The local elections are the first of a series which will culminate in parliamentary elections in September, with a new bicameral parliament being inaugurated by King Hassan on the second Friday of October.
